text.tspan: From the browser to orca-serve on a private EC2 instance
Each boundary checks something different and refuses what does not pass

svg.text: Ends HTTPS and WSS, caches /assets/* only
Checks the cookie on every request,
serves the login and first-setup pages
signing key, read-only for the function
TCP 80 from the CloudFront origin-facing prefix list only
Web UI and runtime RPC (WebSocket) on one port
WebSocket before a password is set: 503
Outside the prefix list: no connection
Outside the ALB security group: no connection

text.tspan: Only requests past the access password reach Orca pairing

svg.text: Checks the cookie on every request: HTML, /assets/* and WebSocket upgrades
A correct password issues the orca_gate cookie, expiry signed with HMAC-SHA256, 7 days
Cookie attributes HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, never forwarded to the origin
Only a browser that opened the pairing link is registered, its device key stays in the browser
RPC is end-to-end encrypted, CloudFront and the ALB carry ciphertext only
A link is single-use (from Orca 1.4.254), every server start prints a new one

text.tspan: Only the pairing link and the setup code remain in plain text

svg.text: CloudFront and the ALB rule use the same dynamic
reference, stack outputs show the ARN only
Plain text is never stored, 8 characters or more
Deleted once a password is set,
Plain text, leave it out of the
The instance role is what an Orca session can use
Terminals and agents run with the instance role, so handle the link and the password like admin credentials
As of 2026-11-22, Orca 1.4.269, based on the code in infra-cdk/lib and the Orca 1.4.254 release notes
